current.title: ALIVE-13 - Reliable Research Retrieval and Evidence-Grounded Connections
current.text:
ALIVE-13 - Reliable Research Retrieval and Evidence-Grounded Connections
What was wrong
ALIVE-12 established the research-memory lifecycle, but its retrieval path was:
goal + current text -> unscoped MemoryService top-k -> post-filter by research metadata
The rank and limit were therefore decided before goal and record-type eligibility. Sixty older ordinary memories could fill the candidate window before the relevant research row was considered. The same shared MemoryService path was also used by general cognition, so a saved research excerpt could enter an ordinary investigation prompt. The panel's withdrawal command used the last saved research ID rather than the displayed result. Lexical overlap was labelled same_concept or complementary, which overstated what shared words establish.
The frozen pre-fix evidence is in archives/ALIVE-13/evidence/pre-fix-defects.json:
With 60 ordinary memories, the old path returned 15 ordinary candidates and zero research candidates; the relevant research memory was absent.
The old general retrieval path returned the research sentinel; the corrected default returned the ordinary experience memory and excluded the sentinel.
The old background worker withdrew research-B-last-saved when the displayed item was research-A-displayed; the corrected worker withdrew the displayed ID and rejected a request with no explicit ID.
Contradictory, unrelated and weakly related fixtures were labelled same_concept, complementary or no_supported_connection; the corrected labels are topic_overlap_candidate, weak_lexical_overlap and insufficient_evidence.
These controlled reproductions reconstruct the pre-fix algorithm against a fresh database: the old query, top-k and post-filter are copied from af12bc8, and the ALIVE-13 type allowlist is explicitly disabled. They are faithful reproductions of the defect, not a literal execution from a checkout made before the edits.

Feedback ratings were scripted operator branch interventions, not a user study.
